dedupe_keys.name: taiwan residential earthquake insurance fund treif open data tables policies premiums claims chi chi damage by district and active faults

description: Taiwan Residential Earthquake Insurance Fund (財團法人住宅地震保險基金, TREIF) publishes seventeen open CSV tables of the residential earthquake insurance fund, including the policies in force against the number of households (a yearly take-up rate rising from 5.99 percent in 2002 to 39.41 percent in 2025), written premium income, claims by earthquake event (date, name, magnitude, number of claims and amount in New Taiwan dollars), the per-county and district damage statistics of the 1999 Chi-Chi (921) earthquake (dead and missing, seriously injured, fully and half collapsed households), a descriptive table of the active faults of Taiwan by region, and tables of world earthquakes with large casualties or magnitude since 1900. Coverage: Taiwan for the insurance and Chi-Chi tables, the world for the earthquake lists; the files carry update dates from 2014 to February 2026. Format and access: CSV files under the fund website open_data path, free and without registration; the open data listing page itself was not found (HTTP 404 at /opendata), so the files were found through links on the fund site. Licence (read on the portal page on 2026-09-29): Not stated on the pages read; cost: free. Caveats: the files are Big5 or CP950 encoded, not UTF-8; no licence is stated on the pages read; the active-fault table is text descriptions without coordinates; the claims table is a summary by event (the file has about 14 rows) and not policy-level; the remaining tables (reserves, governance history, outreach counts) are administrative. Simulation uses: calibrating earthquake insurance take-up, loss and building-damage models for Taiwan, historical damage counts by district for the 1999 event, and fault descriptions as hazard context for seismic risk studies. Related catalogue records: OpenStreetMap (data-openstreetmap).
